project.name: Hackathon Strategist
project.description: Multi-agent hackathon research & ideation system that tells a team what to build to win

layers.name: Application Entry Points
layers.description: CLI and browser bootstrap that load environment/config and start the Strategist orchestrator or the React control-room app

layers.name: Control Room
layers.description: Live operations layer: WebSocket directive broker, HTTP server, and React UI for monitoring the deliberation loop and interjecting mid-run

layers.name: Orchestration Engine
layers.description: Core deliberation orchestration: stage machine, event bus, budget governor, persona task scheduling, and artifact writing that drive a Strategist run

layers.name: Agent Execution
layers.description: LLM provider detection, agent runner, structured output parsing, and tool registration that execute the persona prompts

layers.name: Research Ingestion
layers.description: Ingests sponsor, event, and past-winner research data from HTML and CSV sources to feed the deliberation loop

layers.name: Domain Data & Scoring

nodes.name: runner.ts
nodes.summary: Persona runner that loads persona markdown files, executes them through the LLM with an optional tool-use loop, and returns raw plus parsed JSON output.

nodes.summary: Vitest unit tests for the structured-output coercion helpers (idea cards, findings, verdicts, debate messages, scores) and JSON extraction robustness.

nodes.name: structured.ts
nodes.summary: Lenient coercion of persona LLM JSON into typed domain objects, defaulting missing fields and rejecting garbage entries so the engine never crashes on malformed output.

nodes.name: tools.ts
nodes.summary: Tool registry exposing webFetch, readFile, csvParse, and summarize tools that persona runs can invoke during research.

nodes.name: writer.ts

nodes.name: defaults.ts
nodes.summary: Default values for optional event configuration fields (output directory, concurrency, mode, budgets, gates, team).

nodes.name: env.ts
nodes.summary: Loads .env.local into process.env once at startup (shell exports win) and provides fail-fast access to required environment variables.

nodes.name: types.ts

nodes.name: broker.test.ts

nodes.name: callLLM

nodes.name: salvageTruncatedJSON

nodes.name: loadAllPersonas

nodes.name: findPersona

nodes.name: loadPersona
nodes.summary: Reads a persona markdown file and parses its YAML frontmatter into a PersonaFile.

nodes.name: runPersona
nodes.summary: Runs a persona through the LLM with an optional tool-use loop, parsing JSON output and returning the raw plus parsed result.

nodes.name: runPersonaById

nodes.name: toFindings

nodes.name: toVerdict

nodes.name: toDebateMessages
nodes.summary: Coerces debate JSON into DebateMessage objects with persona fallbacks.

nodes.name: extractCriteria
nodes.summary: Extracts and validates a score-criteria map from a raw record, returning null for non-genuine score objects.

nodes.name: toScores
nodes.summary: Coerces score JSON (array or map form) into typed Score objects, rejecting garbage entries and filtering to known idea IDs.

nodes.name: stripBoilerplate
nodes.summary: Removes script/style/nav/footer/header blocks and HTML tags, collapsing whitespace for webFetch output.

nodes.name: execTool

nodes.name: writeArtifacts

nodes.name: renderImplementationPlan
nodes.summary: Renders the implementation-plan markdown from the run outcome.

nodes.name: renderShortlist
nodes.summary: Renders the Top-3 shortlist table with per-criterion scores.

nodes.name: renderLoopLog
nodes.summary: Renders a chronological log of deliberation rounds for the loop-log artifact.

nodes.name: renderApprovalSheet
nodes.summary: Renders the reviewer approval sheet listing per-reviewer verdicts.

nodes.name: renderDecisionBrief
nodes.summary: Renders the decision brief summarizing the winner, dissent, and weight sensitivity.

nodes.name: loadEnv
nodes.summary: Idempotently loads .env.local into process.env without overwriting existing values.

nodes.name: requireEnv
nodes.summary: Returns a required environment variable or throws with a pointer to .env.local.

nodes.name: validateConfig
nodes.summary: Validates an EventConfig object field-by-field, returning a list of errors (empty when valid).

nodes.summary: Loads and validates an event config JSON file, throwing with all validation errors if invalid.

nodes.name: broker.ts

nodes.name: server.test.ts

nodes.name: components.tsx

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README explains what the Hackathon Strategist is: a multi-agent research and ideation system that ingests an event's website, problem statements, and datasets; researches sponsors, judges, audience, and past winners; generates candidate ideas; and then runs a debate-and-refine loop until a panel of reviewer personas approves a Top 3 and a winning solution. It also maps the runtime: an orchestrator driving staged personas, an event bus streaming to a live React control room, and a set of markdown artifacts (spec.md, implementation-plan.md) as the final deliverable. This is your roadmap for everything that follows.

tour.title: Application Entry Points
tour.description: main.ts is the CLI bootstrap: it loads environment and event configuration, detects the LLM provider, optionally launches the control-room server, runs the Orchestrator, and reports the run outcome. main.tsx is the other face of the system, a thin React entry point that mounts the control-room UI. Together they reveal the project's dual nature - a headless, scriptable pipeline and a live monitoring surface - both funneling into the same engine you will explore next.
tour.languageLesson: main.ts relies on TypeScript ESM top-level await (enabled by "type": "module" in package.json), which lets bootstrap logic run sequentially at module scope instead of being wrapped in an async main() call.

tour.title: Configuration System
tour.description: Every run is driven by configuration, so the entry point's first job is to load it. config/types.ts defines the EventConfig shape - budgets, gates, team, sponsors, and strategy mode - that all engine layers depend on. schema.ts validates the event JSON field-by-field without external libraries, collecting every validation error before throwing. env.ts loads .env.local once and fails fast on missing variables. The example event config is a concrete instance of this schema you can trace through the rest of the tour.
tour.languageLesson: The config layer uses a fail-fast pattern: env.ts reads required variables at import time so a misconfigured deployment crashes at startup with a clear message instead of failing deep inside a run.

tour.title: Domain Data & Scoring
tour.description: data/types.ts is the single most-depended-upon file in the codebase (fan-in of 17), defining the shared vocabulary: personas, stages, idea cards, scores, verdicts, human directives, deliberation rounds, and the event-bus event types that every layer imports. idea-pool.ts provides the in-memory Map storage for candidate idea cards, while scoring.ts implements the weighted scoring engine with ranking, convergence detection, and sensitivity analysis. Understanding this step's types makes every later module far easier to read.
tour.languageLesson: The event types here lean on TypeScript discriminated unions: a shared 'type' discriminant field plus a typed payload lets the event bus switch exhaustively over event kinds, so the compiler catches any unhandled case.

tour.title: Orchestration Engine
tour.description: Orchestrator is the run controller and the hub of the entire system. It drives the staged pipeline - ingest, research, synthesize, ideate, loop, finalize, artifacts - and wires together the persona callbacks, budget governor, event bus, gates, and the control-room server. With a fan-out of 15, it is the broadest-scope module: nearly every other source file is reachable from here, which is exactly why the BFS traversal from main.ts lands on it at depth 1.

tour.title: Run Lifecycle & Deliberation
tour.description: Where the Orchestrator decides what happens, these four modules define how it happens. StageMachine drives the run through ordered stages, emitting a stage event at each transition. EventBus is the single source of truth for run events - its globalBus singleton powers the transcript, loop log, and control-room WebSocket stream. The deliberation-loop owns the iterative debate-to-score-to-review-to-approve cycle, computing the Top 3 and winner when reviewers approve or the budget runs out. BudgetGovernor enforces research time budgets and round caps, giving the loop its stopping conditions.

tour.title: Agent Execution
tour.description: The engine decides what to do, but the personas actually do it - and this step is the machinery in between. persona-tasks.ts (the highest fan-out file in the project) provides the engine-level callbacks that run each persona and coerce its JSON, degrading to deterministic stubs on failure. llm.ts is the multi-provider LLM client (Anthropic SDK, OmniRoute, LiteLLM) with retry logic. runner.ts loads a persona's markdown definition and executes it through the LLM, while structured.ts leniently coerces the model's JSON into the typed domain objects from Step 4. tools.ts registers webFetch, readFile, csvParse, and summarize for research-time tool use.
tour.languageLesson: LLM output is unreliable JSON, so llm.ts uses resilient extraction: it first tries to parse a complete JSON object, then attempts to salvage truncated model output by re-balancing brackets before giving up and letting the persona call degrade to a stub.

tour.title: Agent Personas
tour.description: This is the multi-agent system's brain: the definitions that make each of the 12 personas behave differently. registry.ts scans the .agents/personas directory tree, parsing YAML frontmatter for metadata and providing lookup by slug; the registry.json file declares the persona catalog. The personas themselves are markdown documents - the orchestrator coordinates the run, the data-analyst pursues research, and the judge enforces the rubric - that runner.ts from Step 7 executes as prompts. These documents are the product of the system, in a real sense: they encode the strategy expertise.
tour.languageLesson: Agents are defined as markdown files with YAML frontmatter - the frontmatter holds metadata (slug, role, model, skills) that registry.ts parses, while the body is the persona's system prompt. This keeps agent definitions data-driven and editable without touching TypeScript.

tour.title: Research Ingestion
tour.description: The research personas from Step 8 need raw material, and ingest.ts is how the system gets it. It fetches the event website and rubric and past-winner URLs, normalizes the HTML, reads local data files, caches site content, and flags missing inputs so the run degrades gracefully. parsers/html.ts strips script, style, nav, and footer blocks and collapses whitespace into clean readable text that an LLM can actually consume. This pipeline runs in the first stage of the Orchestrator (Step 5) and feeds the data-analyst personas.

tour.title: Control Room
tour.description: The control room is the live-ops layer first mentioned in the README and launched from main.ts. server.ts serves the built React UI over HTTP and streams event-bus events over WebSocket, accepting human interjections and resolving gates with timeout escalation. broker.ts routes those interjections to the targeted reviewer persona(s). On the frontend, useStrategistStream.ts is the React hook that connects to the WebSocket and accumulates the event stream, while components.tsx renders the stage rail, transcript, score board, verdict panel, and gate controls. This step ties the event bus from Step 6 to a real-time human interface.
tour.languageLesson: The UI uses a single custom hook (useStrategistStream) as the WebSocket bridge: it owns the connection lifecycle, replays the accumulated event history, and exposes derived state plus interject and resolveGate actions - the hook pattern keeps the socket logic out of components entirely.

tour.title: Artifacts & Output
tour.description: After the deliberation loop converges, writer.ts produces the system's actual deliverables: spec.md, implementation plan, executive summary, shortlist, evidence dossier, loop log, approval sheet, and decision brief. The example output documents show what a completed run looks like - the spec that a build team can execute immediately and the decision brief that records how the winning idea was chosen. This is the 'tell us what to build to win' promise from Step 1, made concrete.

tour.title: Build & Deployment
tour.description: package.json ties the project together as a runnable product: it defines the strategist:run CLI script, the React build for the control room, and the test tooling used across the codebase. vercel.json configures deployment of the control-room UI to Vercel, completing the journey from a CLI-driven research pipeline to a deployable web surface.
tour.languageLesson: Because the Strategist runs as a CLI rather than a server, only the control-room UI is deployed; vercel.json uses a rewrite rule so SPA client-side routing falls back to index.html.
